case_facts: My landlord is trying to evict me from my flat with 3 days notice though I've paid rent on time for 5 years.

analysis.summary: A residential tenant of five years' standing faces eviction proceedings initiated by the landlord on only three days' notice, despite a consistent and timely rent-payment history. The core dispute concerns whether such short notice is legally valid and whether the landlord has lawful grounds for eviction. The tenant seeks protection against arbitrary or unlawful dispossession.

issues.issue: Validity of a 3-day eviction notice for a long-standing residential tenant
Minimum statutory notice period required to terminate a month-to-month or yearly residential tenancy
issues.governing_law: Section 106, Transfer of Property Act 1882; applicable State Rent Control Act

issues.issue: Whether consistent timely payment of rent creates a presumption against eviction or estops the landlord from summary eviction
issues.governing_law: State Rent Control Act; Model Tenancy Act 2021

issues.issue: Tenant's right to seek injunction or stay against forcible or unlawful dispossession
issues.governing_law: Order 39 Rules 1 & 2, Code of Civil Procedure 1908; Specific Relief Act 1963

precedents.title: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
precedents.snippet: [DEMO SUMMARY] The Court recognised that the right to livelihood is an integral facet of the right to life. While encroachers can be removed, the procedure must be fair and reasonable, and reasonable notice and an opportunity to be heard must be given before eviction.

precedents.title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
precedents.snippet: [DEMO SUMMARY] In the absence of legislation, the Court framed binding guidelines placing a positive duty on employers to provide a safe working environment and effective complaint mechanisms. The decision illustrates judicially-created obligations filling a statutory gap.

precedents.title: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
precedents.snippet: [DEMO SUMMARY] The Court applied the polluter-pays principle, holding that the financial cost of preventing or remedying damage caused by an activity must be borne by the party responsible for the harm. The principle informs liability and compensation analysis across regulatory disputes.

precedents.snippet: [DEMO SUMMARY] The Court held that a speedy trial is an essential ingredient of the right to life and liberty under Article 21. plan.esql: FROM legal-judgments | WHERE (text LIKE '*eviction*' OR text LIKE '*notice to quit*' OR text LIKE '*Transfer of Property Act*') AND (text LIKE '*tenant*' OR text LIKE '*landlord*' OR text LIKE '*Rent Control*') | KEEP title, headline, catchwords, text, date | LIMIT 10
